subject: general
question: The Lion Capital pillar is located at:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarnath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lion Capital **of **Ashoka **is the **capital**, or **head**, of **a column**, erected by the **Mauryan emperor Ashoka **in **Sarnath**, **India, c. 250 BCE**.
 
• Its **crowning features **are four **life-sized lions **set **back to back **on a **drum-shaped abacus**.
 
• The **national emblem **is **an adaptation of the Lion Capital**, originally found atop the Ashoka Column at Sarnath.
 
• The **capital **has four **Asiatic lions**—**symbolizing power**, **courage**, **pride**, and **confidence—seated.**
 
• **Ashoka the Great**, was an **Indian emperor **of the **Maurya Empire**, son **of Bindusara**.
 
• He **ruled **almost **the entire Indian **subcontinent from c**. 268 to 232 BCE**.
 
• **Ashoka promoted **the spread **of Buddhism across ancient **Asia

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **capital had five components**:

 
 
• The shaft (now broken into many parts)
 
• A lotus base bell.
 
• A drum on the base bell with 4 animals proceeding clockwise (abacus)
 
• Figures of 4 lions.
 
• The crowning part, a large wheel (this is also broken and displayed at the museum)
